Description: Responses to the 948 diagnostic mathematics questions of the NeurIPS 2020 Education Challenge tasks 3 and 4 (question quality and personalisation). Split out from neurips_2020, which holds the tasks 1/2 release: the challenge anonymised the two releases separately and its guide (arXiv:2007.12061, p.8) states that question, user and answer IDs must not be linked between them, so they cannot share an id or item space. resp is 1 if the student answered correctly. See irw#1875.
Reference: Wang, Z., Lamb, A., Saveliev, E., Cameron, P., Zaykov, Y., Hernández-Lobato, J.M., Turner, R.E., Baraniuk, R.G., Barton, C., Jones, S.P., Woodhead, S., & Zhang, C. (2020). Diagnostic questions: The neurips 2020 education challenge [data set]. arXiv preprint arXiv:2007.12061
Notes: Same source download as neurips_2020 (data.zip from eedi.com/research#data): train_task_3_4.csv, test_private_task_4.csv and test_public_task_4_more_splits.csv. Built by data/neurlps_2020.R, which writes both tables. The 948 question IMAGES bundled in the same download are restricted to competition use by the guide (sec. 2.2) and are not redistributed here; only the response records are.

Description: Satisfaction With Life Scale (Diener), 5 items rated 1-7, from a study of how the role of health and emotions in life satisfaction changes at milestone ages. Responses from 810 adults across four sites (Columbus OH, France, Denmark, Austin TX).
Reference: Miron-Shatz, T.; Bhargave, R.; Doniger, G.M. (2015). Milestone Age Affects the Role of Health and Emotions in Life Satisfaction: A Preliminary Inquiry. PLOS ONE, 10(8), e0133254. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0133254

Description: Overall feeling yesterday: 10 mood adjectives (impatient, competent, tense, happy, depressed, interested, affectionate, calm, irritated, tired) each rated 0-6. Duration-weighted recodes of the same adjectives are excluded as composites. Responses from 810 adults across four sites (Columbus OH, France, Denmark, Austin TX).
Reference: Miron-Shatz, T.; Bhargave, R.; Doniger, G.M. (2015). Milestone Age Affects the Role of Health and Emotions in Life Satisfaction: A Preliminary Inquiry. PLOS ONE, 10(8), e0133254. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0133254

Description: Happy, tired and tense/stressed rated 0-6 for each of four day types (typical working weekday, non-working weekday, Sunday, Saturday), 12 items. Sparse by design: the working-weekday items were asked only of respondents in work. Responses from 810 adults across four sites (Columbus OH, France, Denmark, Austin TX).
Reference: Miron-Shatz, T.; Bhargave, R.; Doniger, G.M. (2015). Milestone Age Affects the Role of Health and Emotions in Life Satisfaction: A Preliminary Inquiry. PLOS ONE, 10(8), e0133254. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0133254

Description: Self-description on 12 adjectives (enthusiastic, optimistic, laughs easily, pessimistic, worrier, depressed, often angry, often tense and others), each rated -3 to 3. The pos_self/neg_self averages are excluded as composites. Responses from 810 adults across four sites (Columbus OH, France, Denmark, Austin TX).
Reference: Miron-Shatz, T.; Bhargave, R.; Doniger, G.M. (2015). Milestone Age Affects the Role of Health and Emotions in Life Satisfaction: A Preliminary Inquiry. PLOS ONE, 10(8), e0133254. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0133254

Description: 33 life domains (work, children, friends, financial security, nature, sex, health, travel, art and others) each rated 1-3 as a source of joy. Responses from 810 adults across four sites (Columbus OH, France, Denmark, Austin TX).
Reference: Miron-Shatz, T.; Bhargave, R.; Doniger, G.M. (2015). Milestone Age Affects the Role of Health and Emotions in Life Satisfaction: A Preliminary Inquiry. PLOS ONE, 10(8), e0133254. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0133254

Description: 33 life domains each rated 1-3 as a source of pain. Not the same 33 domains as the joy list: this one includes the politics of the country and hobbies around house & garden where the joy list has creative hobbies, home improvement and future career, so the two are separate tables rather than one merged on an assumed correspondence. Responses from 810 adults across four sites (Columbus OH, France, Denmark, Austin TX).
Reference: Miron-Shatz, T.; Bhargave, R.; Doniger, G.M. (2015). Milestone Age Affects the Role of Health and Emotions in Life Satisfaction: A Preliminary Inquiry. PLOS ONE, 10(8), e0133254. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0133254

Description: Six binary self-ratings against 'most people' (anxious, healthy, reliable and responsible, happy, lucky in life, drives better on the road), coded 0/1. Responses from 810 adults across four sites (Columbus OH, France, Denmark, Austin TX).
Reference: Miron-Shatz, T.; Bhargave, R.; Doniger, G.M. (2015). Milestone Age Affects the Role of Health and Emotions in Life Satisfaction: A Preliminary Inquiry. PLOS ONE, 10(8), e0133254. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0133254

Description: What the respondent wishes most for their child or grandchild, rating cheerful, friendly, polite and intelligent 1-4. Responses from 810 adults across four sites (Columbus OH, France, Denmark, Austin TX).
Reference: Miron-Shatz, T.; Bhargave, R.; Doniger, G.M. (2015). Milestone Age Affects the Role of Health and Emotions in Life Satisfaction: A Preliminary Inquiry. PLOS ONE, 10(8), e0133254. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0133254

Description: Seven statements about the nature of happiness (whether it is difficult to reach, reachable only through love, tied to sharing meals with loved ones, and so on), each rated 1-4. Responses from 810 adults across four sites (Columbus OH, France, Denmark, Austin TX).
Reference: Miron-Shatz, T.; Bhargave, R.; Doniger, G.M. (2015). Milestone Age Affects the Role of Health and Emotions in Life Satisfaction: A Preliminary Inquiry. PLOS ONE, 10(8), e0133254. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0133254

Description: Core Self-Evaluations Scale (Judge et al.), 12 items rated 1-5, from a two-country study of the perception, action and development paths linking core self-evaluations to work engagement. Items are as administered: the deposit's six reverse-keyed recodes are excluded so each item appears once. Responses from 706 employees pooling the paper's two samples, the Netherlands (N=303) and Germany (N=404), distinguished by cov_country.
Reference: Tims, M.; Akkermans, J. (2017). Core self-evaluations and work engagement: Testing a perception, action, and development path. PLOS ONE, 12(8), e0182745. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0182745

Description: Career competencies questionnaire, 21 items rated 1-5 across six dimensions (reflection on motivation, reflection on qualities, networking, professional profiling, work exploration, career control). Responses from 706 employees pooling the paper's two samples, the Netherlands (N=303) and Germany (N=404), distinguished by cov_country.
Reference: Tims, M.; Akkermans, J. (2017). Core self-evaluations and work engagement: Testing a perception, action, and development path. PLOS ONE, 12(8), e0182745. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0182745

Description: Job autonomy, 4 items rated 1-5. The article describes a three-item measure; the deposit carries four columns and all four are shipped. Responses from 706 employees pooling the paper's two samples, the Netherlands (N=303) and Germany (N=404), distinguished by cov_country.
Reference: Tims, M.; Akkermans, J. (2017). Core self-evaluations and work engagement: Testing a perception, action, and development path. PLOS ONE, 12(8), e0182745. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0182745

Description: Supervisory social support, 4 items rated 1-5. The article describes a three-item measure; the deposit carries four columns and all four are shipped. Responses from 706 employees pooling the paper's two samples, the Netherlands (N=303) and Germany (N=404), distinguished by cov_country.
Reference: Tims, M.; Akkermans, J. (2017). Core self-evaluations and work engagement: Testing a perception, action, and development path. PLOS ONE, 12(8), e0182745. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0182745

Description: Job Crafting Scale (Tims et al.), the 15 expansive items rated 1-5 across three dimensions: increasing structural job resources, increasing social job resources, and increasing challenging job demands. Responses from 706 employees pooling the paper's two samples, the Netherlands (N=303) and Germany (N=404), distinguished by cov_country.
Reference: Tims, M.; Akkermans, J. (2017). Core self-evaluations and work engagement: Testing a perception, action, and development path. PLOS ONE, 12(8), e0182745. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0182745

Description: Hindering job demands, 6 items rated 1-5. Responses from 706 employees pooling the paper's two samples, the Netherlands (N=303) and Germany (N=404), distinguished by cov_country.
Reference: Tims, M.; Akkermans, J. (2017). Core self-evaluations and work engagement: Testing a perception, action, and development path. PLOS ONE, 12(8), e0182745. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0182745

Description: Utrecht Work Engagement Scale (UWES-9), 9 items rated 1-7 across vigor, dedication and absorption. Responses from 706 employees pooling the paper's two samples, the Netherlands (N=303) and Germany (N=404), distinguished by cov_country.
Reference: Tims, M.; Akkermans, J. (2017). Core self-evaluations and work engagement: Testing a perception, action, and development path. PLOS ONE, 12(8), e0182745. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0182745

Description: Teacher work values scale (Xu Xingchun), 27 items rated 1-5 across seven dimensions: material remuneration, reputation and status, career development, interpersonal relations, organizational management, altruistic dedication, and security and stability. Responses from 873 primary and secondary school teachers in Guangdong Province, China.
Reference: Feng, G.; Shi, K.; Huang, Q.; Ma, J. (2024). The impact of work values on the professional development of primary and secondary school teachers: A moderated mediation model. PLOS ONE, 19(11), e0310078. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0310078

Description: Professional development of primary and secondary school teachers (Chen Jingjun et al.), 21 items rated 1-5 across five dimensions: professional sentiment, development actions, professionalization concept, problem-solving skills, and professional knowledge. Responses from 873 primary and secondary school teachers in Guangdong Province, China.
Reference: Feng, G.; Shi, K.; Huang, Q.; Ma, J. (2024). The impact of work values on the professional development of primary and secondary school teachers: A moderated mediation model. PLOS ONE, 19(11), e0310078. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0310078

Description: Utrecht Work Engagement Scale, Chinese version (Zhang Yiwen & Gan Yiqun), 17 items rated 1-5. Responses from 873 primary and secondary school teachers in Guangdong Province, China.
Reference: Feng, G.; Shi, K.; Huang, Q.; Ma, J. (2024). The impact of work values on the professional development of primary and secondary school teachers: A moderated mediation model. PLOS ONE, 19(11), e0310078. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0310078

Description: Perceived organizational support, 24 items rated 1-5. Responses from 873 primary and secondary school teachers in Guangdong Province, China.
Reference: Feng, G.; Shi, K.; Huang, Q.; Ma, J. (2024). The impact of work values on the professional development of primary and secondary school teachers: A moderated mediation model. PLOS ONE, 19(11), e0310078. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0310078

Description: College student self-control scale (Tan Shuhua), 19 items rated 1-5 across five dimensions: impulse control, healthy habits, resistance to temptation, work concentration and moderate entertainment. Responses from 490 college students at four universities in Hubei Province, China.
Reference: Shen, Q.; Li, L.; Li, C. (2026). How does self-control influences college students’ smartphone dependence: The chain mediating effect of mental toughness and social adaptability. PLOS ONE, 21(6), e0350219. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0350219

Description: Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale, Chinese version, 25 items rated 0-4 across optimism, strength and resilience; reported in the source as mental toughness. Responses from 490 college students at four universities in Hubei Province, China.
Reference: Shen, Q.; Li, L.; Li, C. (2026). How does self-control influences college students’ smartphone dependence: The chain mediating effect of mental toughness and social adaptability. PLOS ONE, 21(6), e0350219. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0350219

Description: Social adaptability diagnostic scale (Zheng Richang), 20 items scored -2, 0 or 2. Left as administered: the source reverses the odd-numbered items before summing, but reverse-scored items are not recoded in IRW. Responses from 490 college students at four universities in Hubei Province, China.
Reference: Shen, Q.; Li, L.; Li, C. (2026). How does self-control influences college students’ smartphone dependence: The chain mediating effect of mental toughness and social adaptability. PLOS ONE, 21(6), e0350219. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0350219

Description: Adult Smartphone Addiction Scale (Chen Huan), rated 1-5. The article describes 20 items; the deposit carries 26 on the same scale with no missing values, and all 26 are shipped. Responses from 490 college students at four universities in Hubei Province, China.
Reference: Shen, Q.; Li, L.; Li, C. (2026). How does self-control influences college students’ smartphone dependence: The chain mediating effect of mental toughness and social adaptability. PLOS ONE, 21(6), e0350219. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0350219

Description: Hierarchical plateau, the 4-item brief career plateau measure (Allen et al.), rated 1-5. Responses from 307 civil servants in the Pearl River Delta, Guangdong Province, China.
Reference: Xiao, L. (2024). The impact of hierarchical plateau on civil servants’ taking charge behavior: The role of work engagement and trait mindfulness. PLOS ONE, 19(12), e0315916. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0315916

Description: Utrecht Work Engagement Scale (UWES-9), 9 items rated 1-5. Responses from 307 civil servants in the Pearl River Delta, Guangdong Province, China.
Reference: Xiao, L. (2024). The impact of hierarchical plateau on civil servants’ taking charge behavior: The role of work engagement and trait mindfulness. PLOS ONE, 19(12), e0315916. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0315916

Description: Mindful Attention Awareness Scale (MAAS), 15 items rated 1-6. Responses from 307 civil servants in the Pearl River Delta, Guangdong Province, China.
Reference: Xiao, L. (2024). The impact of hierarchical plateau on civil servants’ taking charge behavior: The role of work engagement and trait mindfulness. PLOS ONE, 19(12), e0315916. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0315916

Description: Taking charge behavior, the 4 highest-loading items of the Morrison & Phelps scale as used by Parker & Collins, rated 1-5. Responses from 307 civil servants in the Pearl River Delta, Guangdong Province, China.
Reference: Xiao, L. (2024). The impact of hierarchical plateau on civil servants’ taking charge behavior: The role of work engagement and trait mindfulness. PLOS ONE, 19(12), e0315916. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0315916

Description: Leader support for work-family balance, 9 items rated 1 (never) to 5 (very often), following Shinn et al. Item codes LS01-LS09 are positional: the deposit has no item codes, only the full item stems as column headers. Responses from 247 Slovenian employees.
Reference: Žnidaršič, J.; Bernik, M. (2021). Impact of work-family balance results on employee work engagement within the organization: The case of Slovenia. PLOS ONE, 16(1), e0245078. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0245078

Description: Co-worker support for work-family balance: the same 9 items as the leader-support block, re-asked about colleagues, rated 1-5. Item codes CS01-CS09 are positional. Responses from 247 Slovenian employees.
Reference: Žnidaršič, J.; Bernik, M. (2021). Impact of work-family balance results on employee work engagement within the organization: The case of Slovenia. PLOS ONE, 16(1), e0245078. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0245078

Description: Organizational work-family practices, 25 items rated 1-5, drawn from the Slovenian Family-Friendly Company certificate measure set across eight areas including working time, work organization, workplace flexibility, leadership and services for families. Item codes OP01-OP25 are positional. Responses from 247 Slovenian employees.
Reference: Žnidaršič, J.; Bernik, M. (2021). Impact of work-family balance results on employee work engagement within the organization: The case of Slovenia. PLOS ONE, 16(1), e0245078. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0245078

Description: Work-family balance, 4 items rated 1-5 (Brough et al.). Responses from 247 Slovenian employees.
Reference: Žnidaršič, J.; Bernik, M. (2021). Impact of work-family balance results on employee work engagement within the organization: The case of Slovenia. PLOS ONE, 16(1), e0245078. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0245078

Description: Utrecht Work Engagement Scale (UWES-9), 9 items rated 1-5. Responses from 247 Slovenian employees.
Reference: Žnidaršič, J.; Bernik, M. (2021). Impact of work-family balance results on employee work engagement within the organization: The case of Slovenia. PLOS ONE, 16(1), e0245078. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0245078

Description: Revised UCLA Loneliness Scale (R-UCLA), 20 items rated 1-4. Responses from 200 Polish migrants living in the UK.
Reference: Tatala, M.; Wojtasiński, M.; Janowski, K. (2023). Loneliness and time abroad in Polish migrants in the UK: Protective role of religious experience. PLOS ONE, 18(2), e0279984. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0279984
